claims.claim: An action upon a contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing must be brought within four years.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: Four years is the general rule. Section 337(a) expressly excepts §336a and sets a three-month post-sale limit for certain actions to recover a secured balance.

claims.claim: Once the applicable §337 period has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate arbitration or another legal proceeding to collect the debt.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt.
claims.note: The bar applies to each listed proceeding.

claims.claim: The §337 period can be extended only under Section 360.
claims.quote: The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.
claims.note: Section 337(d) names §360 as the sole basis for extension.

claims.claim: The answer must contain a statement of any new matter constituting a defense.
claims.quote:
(b) The answer to a complaint shall contain:
(1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.
(2) A statement of any new matter constituting a defense.
claims.note: This is a general requirement for an answer; the quoted provision does not specifically identify a limitations defense.

flags.text: The unqualified four-year statement omits the §336a exception and the three-month limit after a power-of-sale sale for an action seeking the balance of an obligation secured by the specified deed of trust or mortgage.
The draft gives a duration but no starting point. The provided §337(a) text does not specify when the period begins for an ordinary written-contract claim.

The bare §360 reference does not explain its signed-writing rule or its payment exception: a qualifying principal or interest payment on a promissory note starts a new period, but the payment alone cannot revive an already barred claim.

result.summary: The sources support the collection bar, the §360 cross-reference, and the answer requirement. They support four years as a general rule, not a deadline for every debt founded on a writing.
